- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or bullish sentiment; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < 0.20), model tends to underestimate, so adjust forecast downward by 3–8% for 3–5 day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% per day post-spike if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., > 0.70) and price is trending up, model may overfit recent momentum; cap forecast growth at 1–2% per day unless sentiment is sustained.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model shows steady upward trend but true outcome shows sharp decline, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days if sentiment is weak.
- Sentiment history with multiple negative values (e.g., -0.14, -0.20) correlates with underestimation; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is negative but not extreme.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows a “tail” or late surge (e.g., 58.80, 61.42, 61.50), model often misses it; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
